body:
A patch for this, on a branch — it follows the reporter's four requirements, and the isolated loopback setup here mirrors the reporter's own (credit to kylefu8 for the precise spec and the measurements). **What's wrong.** A long session of screenshots pushes the request past a vendor's byte cap while the tokens still fit the model's window, and every turn is refused from then on. The plugin chain is no guarantee: as the reporter measured (34,603,056 bytes reaching a simulated upstream with the async hook and the sync middleware both failing), a plugin that fails or times out stands aside and the whole body goes out anyway. Nothing native checks the final size. **Root cause.** The gateway has no surface for a per-provider cap on the bytes of one request as they actually go out. What exists acts on the model's token window (context fitting, the refit-smaller path) or inside plugins; no code measures the final body at the send site, so an over-cap body is always handed to the vendor and refused after the fact. **The fix** (fork branch [`fix/4282-body-size-limit`](https://github.com/ggbdpq/magpie/tree/fix/4282-body-size-limit), head `c45499dd0ceb952b71a4a5a135bcd0c46f98c866`): - `provider.BodyLimit`, off by default (0), per provider, clamped to at most 1 GiB. Set with `magpie provider body-limit 28mib` — plain bytes or kb/kib/mb/mib/gib, `off` takes it away. - Checked in `forwardOnce` immediately before `provider.SetBody` hands the body to the transport — after every plugin, route, protocol translation and context fitting has had its say. As the reporter asked, the metered layer is defined: it is the raw body handed to the transport, the plain bytes, counted before the zstd compression a Codex wire turn applies — the larger side of what the vendor receives. - Over the limit, the request is refused locally with a 413 typed `request_too_large`, which says the size, the limit and where the limit is set. The provider is asked nothing (the tests assert 0 upstream calls), the body is not truncated, and the refusal is not acted on as a vendor word: it is marked so the refit-smaller path doesn't fit the body and ask again, and the fallback loop doesn't hand the body to another provider (serve reads the refusal's own words, the way `restrictedSaid` reads magpie's own words elsewhere). The provider is not rested by it either. - A plugin that fails or times out cannot bypass the check: it sits after the whole plugin chain, whatever the plugins did. - The GUI editor doesn't show the limit; a save keeps what it was set to.
patch (0001, 562 insertions, 10 files — also at 0001-gateway-a-provider-s-own-limit-on-the-bytes-of.patch on the branch) ```diff From c45499dd0ceb952b71a4a5a135bcd0c46f98c866 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001 From: ggbdpq Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 01:14:15 +0800 Subject: [PATCH] gateway: a provider's own limit on the bytes of one request, refused here (#4282) MIME-Version: 1.0 Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8 Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit A long session of screenshots can pass a vendor's byte cap while its tokens still fit the model's window, and then every turn is refused and the session can neither go on nor compact. The images a plugin shrinks are no guarantee: a plugin that fails, or times out, stands aside and the whole body goes (the reporter measured 34.6 MB reach an upstream that way). So a provider takes a BodyLimit, off by default, set with `magpie provider body-limit 28mib` (bytes, or kb/kib/mb/mib/gib, off to take it away; at most a GiB). forwardOnce measures the body as it goes out — after every plugin, route, translation and fitting has had its say, the bytes provider.SetBody hands the transport, the Content-Length on the wire. A body over the limit is refused with a 413 said here, which says the size and the limit: the provider is asked nothing, the body is not cut, and the request is not sent again — the refusal is marked so refitOverCap doesn't read it as the vendor's word and fit the body smaller to ask again, and it is not handed to the provider's fallback either: the limit is the user's own word for this provider, and the body never went out (serve reads the refusal's own words, as restrictedSaid does). A turn to a Codex account goes zstd-compressed on the wire; the limit counts it before that compression, the plain bytes, the larger and so safer side of what the vendor receives. The editor doesn't show the limit; a save keeps what it was set to, as it keeps the rest cap. Fixes #4282 Generated-by: GLM-5.3-Flash (ZCode) --- internal/cli/body_limit_cli_test.go | 51 +++++++ internal/cli/providers_cli.go | 79 ++++++++++ internal/gateway/body_limit.go | 72 ++++++++++ internal/gateway/body_limit_test.go | 207 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++ internal/gateway/gateway.go | 20 ++- internal/gui/body_limit_save_test.go | 41 ++++++ internal/gui/providers.go | 5 + internal/provider/body_limit.go | 27 ++++ internal/provider/body_limit_test.go | 57 ++++++++ internal/provider/provider.go | 7 + 10 files changed, 562 insertions(+), 4 deletions(-) create mode 100644 internal/cli/body_limit_cli_test.go create mode 100644 internal/gateway/body_limit.go create mode 100644 internal/gateway/body_limit_test.go create mode 100644 internal/gui/body_limit_save_test.go create mode 100644 internal/provider/body_limit.go create mode 100644 internal/provider/body_limit_test.go diff --git a/internal/cli/body_limit_cli_test.go b/internal/cli/body_limit_cli_test.go new file mode 100644 index 000000000..d4afb4015 --- /dev/null +++ b/internal/cli/body_limit_cli_test.go @@ -0,0 +1,51 @@ +package cli + +import ( + "testing" + + "github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/provider" +) + +// #4282: `magpie provider body-limit 28mib` sets the most bytes one +// request to the provider may take, a plain number counts bytes, and off +// takes the limit away. +func TestBodyLimitCmd(t *testing.T) { + home := t.TempDir() + t.Setenv("HOME", home) + t.Setenv("USERPROFILE", home) + t.Setenv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", t.TempDir()) + if err := provider.Save(provider.Provider{ID: "xk", Name: "xk", Chat: "https://example.invalid/v1", Key: "k"}); err != nil { + t.Fatal(err) + } + limit := func() int { + p, err := provider.Find("xk") + if err != nil { + t.Fatal(err) + } + return p.BodyLimit + } + if err := bodyLimitCmd([]string{"xk", "28mib"}); a body over it is refused here and the provider asked + nothing (off: no limit) magpie provider listed yes|no no: its models serve only through routing groups, not in the list magpie provider off|on switch it off (kept, but no agent or request uses it), or on again magpie provider test [--as codex|claude-code] [model…] @@ -655,6 +660,8 @@ func providerCmd(args []string) error { return quotaRestCmd(rest) case "rest-cap": return restCapCmd(rest) + case "body-limit": + return bodyLimitCmd(rest) case "listed": // no: the provider's models leave the list agents see and serve // only through the routing groups they are in @@ -2028,6 +2035,78 @@ func restCapMinutes(s string) (int, error) { return restMinutes(s) } +// bodyLimitCmd reads and sets the most bytes one request to a provider +// may take (#4282): `magpie provider body-limit ` says it, ` +// 28mib` sets it, ` off` takes it away. +func bodyLimitCmd(rest []string) error { + if len(rest) < 1 || len(rest) > 2 { + return fmt.Errorf("magpie provider body-limit [28mib|512kb|2048|off]") + } + p, err := provider.Find(rest[0]) + if err != nil { + return err + } + if len(rest) > 1 { + n, err := bodyLimitBytes(rest[1]) + if err != nil { + return err + } + if err := provider.SetBodyLimit(p.ID, n); err != nil { + return err + } + if p, err = provider.Find(p.ID); err != nil { + return err + } + } + if p.BodyLimit > 0 { + fmt.Printf("%s · one request to it takes at most %s, as it goes out; a body over it is refused here, the provider asked nothing (`magpie provider body-limit %s off` takes it away)\n", p.Name, sizeWords(p.BodyLimit), p.ID) + } else { + fmt.Printf("%s · requests of any size go to it (magpie's own)\n", p.Name) + } + return nil +} + +// bodyLimitSize reads a size as bodyLimitCmd takes it: a number of +// bytes, or the unit named — 2048, 512kb, 28mib. A kb is a KiB, as a +// vendor counts a stated "32 MB … (33554432 bytes)". +var bodyLimitSize = regexp.MustCompile(`^(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*(b|bytes|kb|kib|mb|mib|gb|gib)?$`) + +// bodyLimitBytes is the bytes bodyLimitSize read. +func bodyLimitBytes(s string) (int, error) { + s = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(s)) + switch s { + case "off", "default", "none", "-", "0": + return 0, nil + } + m := bodyLimitSize.FindStringSubmatch(s) + if m == nil { + return 0, fmt.Errorf("the body limit is a number of bytes or a size (28mib, 512kb), or off, not %q", s) + } + f, err := strconv.ParseFloat(m[1], 64) + if err != nil || f < 0 { + return 0, fmt.Errorf("the body limit is a size, not %q", s) + } + unit := map[string]float64{"": 1, "b": 1, "bytes": 1, "kb": 1 << 10, "kib": 1 << 10, "mb": 1 << 20, "mib": 1 << 20, "gb": 1 << 30, "gib": 1 << 30}[m[2]] + if n := f * unit; n > float64(provider.MaxBodyLimit) { + return 0, fmt.Errorf("the most a body limit may be is %s (%d bytes), not %q", sizeWords(provider.MaxBodyLimit), provider.MaxBodyLimit, s) + } else { + return int(n), nil + } +} + +// sizeWords says a number of bytes as a size: 1.0 MB, 28.0 MiB. +func sizeWords(n int) string { + switch { + case n >= 1<<30 && n%(1<<30) == 0: + return fmt.Sprintf("%d GiB", n>>30) + case n >= 1<<20 && n%(1<<20) == 0: + return fmt.Sprintf("%d MiB", n>>20) + case n >= 1<<10 && n%(1<<10) == 0: + return fmt.Sprintf("%d KiB", n>>10) + } + return fmt.Sprintf("%d bytes", n) +} + // restMinutes reads a rest as quotaRestCmd takes it: default (0), a // number of minutes, a Go duration (90m, 6h) or a number of days (7d). func restMinutes(s string) (int, error) { diff --git a/internal/gateway/body_limit.go b/internal/gateway/body_limit.go new file mode 100644 index 000000000..0d365bcce --- /dev/null +++ b/internal/gateway/body_limit.go @@ -0,0 +1,72 @@ +package gateway + +import ( + "bytes" + "encoding/json" + "fmt" + "io" + "net/http" + + "github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/provider" +) + +// A provider's own cap on the bytes of one request, as it goes out +// (issue #4282, kylefu8). A long session of images can pass a vendor's +// byte cap while its tokens still fit the model's window, and every turn +// of it is refused from then on; the images a plugin shrinks are no +// guarantee, a plugin that fails or times out standing aside. So the +// user sets a limit per provider, and forwardOnce measures the request +// after every plugin, route, translation and fitting has had its say — +// the bytes provider.SetBody hands the transport, the Content-Length on +// the wire. A body over the limit is refused with a 413 said here: the +// provider is asked nothing, the body is not cut, and the request is not +// sent again, fitted or otherwise. A turn to a Codex account goes +// zstd-compressed on the wire; the limit counts it before that +// compression, the plain bytes, which is the larger and so the safer +// side of what the vendor receives. + +// bodyLimitMark marks, for the moment forward reads it, the 413 said +// here for a body over the provider's BodyLimit. It comes off at once: +// the vendor's learned byte cap (refitOverCap) would fit such a body +// smaller and ask again, and this request never went out. +const bodyLimitMark = "Magpie-Body-Limit" + +// refusedForBodyLimit says whether res is the 413 said here for a body +// over the provider's BodyLimit, and takes its mark off. +func refusedForBodyLimit(res *http.Response) bool { + if res == nil || res.Header.Get(bodyLimitMark) == "" { + return false + } + res.Header.Del(bodyLimitMark) + return true +} + +// bodyLimitWords is what that 413 calls itself: the one phrase no vendor +// says, by which the refusal is known again where it lands (as +// restrictedSaid knows magpie's own words of a restricted account). +const bodyLimitWords = "the provider's body limit, `magpie provider body-limit`" + +// bodyLimitSaid says a refusal is the 413 said here for a body over the +// provider's BodyLimit, read from its words. serve reads it to keep the +// refusal from being handed to another member: the limit is the user's +// own word for this provider, and the body never went out, so there is +// nothing of it for another to take. +func bodyLimitSaid(body []byte) bool { + return bytes.Contains(body, []byte(bodyLimitWords)) +} + +// bodyLimitRefusal is that 413: the size, the limit, and where the limit +// is set, said as a request_too_large so a client that compacts on one b/internal/gateway/body_limit_test.go new file mode 100644 index 000000000..ad8c38716 --- /dev/null +++ b/internal/gateway/body_limit_test.go @@ -0,0 +1,207 @@ +package gateway + +import ( + "io" + code != 200 { + t.Fatalf("at the size it goes out at exactly, answered %d: %.400s", code, said) + } + if n := len(up3.calls()); n != 1 { + t.Fatalf("the upstream was asked %d times", n) + } +} + +// The refusal is not handed to the provider's fallback: the limit is the +// user's own word for this provider, the body never went out, and no +// other provider is asked for it — nothing is retried, nothing switches +// (issue #4282). hostB.Close() }) + p := provider.Provider{ID: "fake", Name: "1017dp", Key: "k", Models: []string{"m1"}, BodyLimit: 1 << 20, Fallback: []string{"fake2/m1"}, Responses: hostA.URL + "/v1"} + if err := provider.Save(p); err != nil { + t.Fatal(err) + } + p2 := provider.Provider{ID: "fake2", Name: "1017dp2", Key: "k", Models: []string{"m1"}, Responses: hostB.URL + "/v1"} + if err := provider.Save(p2); err != nil { + t.Fatal(err) + } + code, said := post(t, "/v1/responses", longTurn(300_000)) + if code != http.StatusRequestEntityTooLarge { + t.Fatalf("answered %d: %.400s", code, said) + } + if !strings.Contains(said, "body limit") { + t.Errorf("the refusal doesn't say it is the body limit: %.400s", said) + } + if n := len(upA.calls()); n != 0 { + t.Fatalf("the limited provider was asked %d times", n) + } + if n := len(upB.calls()); n != 0 { + t.Fatalf("the fallback was asked for a body the limit refused, %d times, and answered it", n) + } +} + +// postAnthropic asks the gateway's /v1/messages as Claude Code does. +func postAnthropic(t *testing.T, body string) (int, string) { + t.Helper() + rec := httptest.NewRecorder() + req := httptest.NewRequest("POST", "/v1/messages", strings.NewReader(body)) + req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json") + req.Header.Set("anthropic-version", "2023-06-01") + New().Handler().ServeHTTP(rec, req) + return rec.Code, rec.Body.String() +} diff --git a/internal/gateway/gateway.go b/internal/gateway/gateway.go index 757d55393..15486b6b5 100644 --- a/internal/gateway/gateway.go +++ b/internal/gateway/gateway.go @@ -4134,7 +4134,7 @@ func (s *Server) serve(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, from provider.Pro break } } - if !last && !hw.passing && !hw.refused && (hw.code() == http.StatusRequestEntityTooLarge || overflowed(hw.code(), hw.errBody())) { + if !last && !hw.passing && !hw.refused && !bodyLimitSaid(hw.errBody()) && (hw.code() == http.StatusRequestEntityTooLarge || overflowed(hw.code(), hw.errBody())) { // too long for this member's model, and as long on every // account of it, but another member — another model, or this // one at another vendor — may hold it (#700: the overflow went @@ -4142,7 +4142,10 @@ func (s *Server) serve(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, from provider.Pro // window, where the next member would have answered). Only // those not known to be too small are left to ask; none, and // the agent is told, to compact. A byte cap (413) also belongs - // to this member: another vendor may take the same body.
